records.name: cf2024-1._domainkey.harborline.example
records.value: (DKIM key generated by Cloudflare when Email Routing is enabled)
records.note: Created automatically by Email Routing; copy it from the dashboard if adding by hand.

records.name: cf-bounce._domainkey.harborline.example
records.value: (DKIM key generated by Cloudflare when the sending domain is added)
records.note: Shown under Email Sending → domain → DNS records.

records.name: _dmarc.harborline.example
records.note: Only if the domain has no DMARC record yet. Never publish two.

manualSteps: Add harborline.example to Cloudflare (DNS must be on Cloudflare) if it is not already a zone.
Dashboard → harborline.example → Email → Email Routing → Enable. Let it add the MX, SPF and DKIM records.
Email Routing → Routing rules → Catch-all address → Action "Send to a Worker" → cloudmail → Save, and make sure it is enabled.
Email → Email Sending → Add domain → harborline.example. Add the cf-bounce MX/TXT and DKIM records it lists.
If harborline.example has no DMARC record, add TXT _dmarc.harborline.example = "v=DMARC1; p=reject;". If one exists, keep it.
Back here, press "Re-check DNS" until every row passes.

emails.subject: Re: Missed alerts during Saturday's outage (Lumen Health)
emails.body:
Hi Oskar,

I'm sorry. This one is on us. Alert webhooks were queued behind one customer's slow endpoint, so yours waited for retries that should never have blocked them. We shipped a fix on Sunday that gives every workspace its own queue.

emails.subject: How does Fernhill Cloud find out it's down?
emails.body:
Hi Tess,

Your status page showed an incident on the 9th that was posted 35 minutes after customers started tweeting about it. That gap is the thing we fix: Northwind opens the incident, pages on-call and updates the status page from the same alert.

Worth 15 minutes to see it on your own monitors?

Daniel Reyes
Northwind

emails.subject: Re: Webhook signature check failing
emails.body:
Buongiorno Luca,

Please leave the check on. A mismatch on some requests usually means the body is parsed before it is verified, so the bytes differ. Verify against the raw request body and it should pass every time. If it doesn't, send me one failing request id and I'll trace it.

Bea

presets.prompt: Unsolicited sales pitches from people I have never talked to: sales, SEO, development and agency offers, link building, lead generation, guest posts, partnership and sponsorship offers.

presets.name: Spam
presets.prompt: Spam, phishing and scams: unsolicited bulk mail, fake invoices, account or password warnings, prize, loan or crypto offers, malware links, and mail impersonating a brand, bank or service.
